correctness.rationale: The OU difference noise has stationary variance 2 lambda D. Pathwise strict contraction yields a unique stationary log-ratio. Both total- and geometric-growth logarithms yield g=(M/2)E(cosh X-1)=(1/2)E[H tanh(X/2)]. Gaussian integration by parts with the exact causal response exp(-M integral cosh X) proves g=(lambda D/2) integral exp(-lambda u) E[sech^2(X0/2) response] du and strict cap lambda D/[2(M+lambda)]. Stationary X^2, cosh X and XH budgets justify integrability and the quantitative small-M bound. Dominated convergence proves weak-noise and high-M sharpness. Continuity and endpoint limits give interior attainment. The standalone simulator was replayed; no finite experiment is used as an infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: A 2026 ecological study reports only a numerical interior optimum under colored environmental noise. This theorem supplies a rigorous strictly positive benefit for any finite positive migration, a sharp explicit universal growth ceiling, a high-M asymptotic constant, a quantitative low-M suppression estimate, and existence of a genuine optimum in the original non-Markov-in-ratio colored-noise system. The output is a structural all-parameter theorem for an ecologically motivated observable rather than a routine numerical computation.
